items.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
items.summary: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have been climbing following an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers But the Nasdaq Composite opened up on Friday and flattened out around 1.7% higher by lunchtime, reversing some of its 5.5% fall The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, was around 0.9% higher by lunchtime.

items.title: Movement of tourists increases by 254 percent
items.summary: Maputo, 06 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has revealed that the movement of tourists and investors arriving in the country increased by 254 percent this year, when compared to the same period in 2025. According to Chapo, speaking at the opening of the second edition of the Mozambique Tourism Summit, in Vilankulo, southern province of Inhambane, the growth is the result of reforms introduced to boost the tourism sector. “The results stem from measures introduced in recent months to facilitate the entry of visitors and attract investment, including the implementation of an electronic visa platform and the creation of the so-called “Visa Gold”, designed to attract foreign investors”, he said. The President highlighted the creation of the National Agency for Tourism Development and Investment (Anditur), which replaced the former National Tourism Institute (Inatur), as well as the Southern Corridor Special Tourism Economic Zone, which incorporates the destinations of Vilankulo, Pomene and Inhassoro, all in Inhambane province.

items.title: Weather Alert: INAM warns heatwave to continue in Manica and Tete provinces in central Mozambique
items.summary: According to INAM, the continued flow of hot and humid air is causing a heatwave to persist across the central and inland parts of the country The heatwave affects specific areas in two provinces in the central region In Manica province, the warning covers the districts of Guro, Tambara, Macossa, Barué, Vanduzi, Manica, Macate, Sussundenga, Gondola, Mossurize and Machaze , as well as the city of Chimoio In Tete province , the heatwave affects the districts of Magoe, Cahora-Bassa, Changara, Marara, Doa and Mutarara, as well as Tete city In these areas, temperatures could range between 7 and 43 degrees Celsius until 8 November The bulletin highlights that a change in weather conditions is expected on Saturday, 7 November, with thunderstorms, showers or rain, and gusty winds In addition, INAM forecasts a sharp drop in temperatures on Sunday, 8 November, affecting the southern part of the country, particularly Maputo and Gaza provinces In view of the high temperatures forecast, INAM reiterates the need for the public in the affected regions to take precautionary measures The next…

items.summary: Iran is stepping up attacks on shipping in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. items.title: Number of detainees in connection with bishop’s murder rises to five
items.summary: Maputo, 06 Nov (AIM) – The number of suspects detained in connection with the murder of Osório Citora Afonso, Bishop of the Diocese of Quelimane, in the central Mozambican province of Zambézia, has risen from four to five. Bishop Osório Afonso, who was also Apostolic Administrator of the Archdiocese of Beira, in the central province of Sofala, was shot dead last June with an AKM-type firearm. Among the suspects, there are two Catholic priests, a guard employed by the Quelimane Diocese and two civilians. According Fred Jamal, Chief Prosecutor Zambezia Province, speaking to reports, on Thursday, as part of Legal Awareness Day, investigations are underway, especially to identify the perpetrators who physically carried out the murder. “Fortunately, the extension of the preventive detention period gives us more time to carry out our work properly, since it has been extended to 12 months. Work is underway to identify the material perpetrators.

items.title: Zambia's civil service overhaul raises questions
items.summary: Government-backed dismissals and restructuring are fueling debate in Zambia. Opposition politicians are questioning the transparency of the plans; officials say the changes are necessary Many people living in Zambia seek careers in the civil service because of the stability and security traditionally associated with government employment. But recent retirements, dismissals and restructuring exercises across several public institutions have unsettled that perception and sparked a national debate about the government's use of "national interest" provisions Among those affected is former public relations officer Godfrey Chilabi, whose departure from the Zambia Police Service was announced in October. Choosing not to publicly discuss the circumstances surrounding his exit, Chilabi simply told media that he had been retired in the national interest "Yes, I have been retired in national interest," Chilabi said.

items.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a political crisis and a standoff between the presidency and judiciary Thursday's ruling came a day after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed - a move which the court said the president lacked the authority to take The court also ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, potentially disrupting government plans for nationwide polls next year Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May, but his administration extended it by a year through law changes approved by parliament in March Opposition groups accuse him of using the constitutional changes to prolong his rule But the president insists the reforms are necessary to move Somalia towards fully democratic elections, replacing the clan-based system in which elders pick their representatives which has been used since 2012 Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 and has…
